{{Short description|German physicist and science historian}}

'''Helmut Rechenberg''' (6 November 1937, [[Berlin]] – 10 November 2016, [[Munich]]) was a German physicist and science historian.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|date=November 16, 2016|title=Zum Gedenken an Helmut Rechenberg|url=https://www.mpp.mpg.de/aktuelles/meldungen/detail/zum-gedenken-an-helmut-rechenberg|access-date=November 28, 2021|website=www.mpp.mpg.de|language=de-DE}}</ref>

== Biography ==

=== Education ===
Rechenberg studied mathematics, physics and astronomy at [[LMU Munich]] and graduated in 1964. At LMU Munich, his work was in experimental physics, studying the magnetism of solids. He moved to the [[Max Planck Institute for Physics]] in Munich, where he became [[Werner Heisenberg]]'s doctoral student. In 1968, he graduated with a doctorate on [[quantum field theory]]. 

=== Career ===
From 1970 to 1972, he worked at the [[University of Texas at Austin]], collaborating with [[George Sudarshan]] on quantum field theory and with [[Jagdish Mehra]] on science history. He then returned to Germany and the Max Planck Institute, from which he officially retired in 2002.<ref name=":0" />

His six-volume work with [[Jagdish Mehra]] on the history of quantum mechanics has been described as "an extraordinary amount of painstaking scholarship".<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Schweber|first=Silvan S.|author-link=Silvan S. Schweber|date=November 2001|title=The Historical Development of Quantum Theory. Volume 6: The Completion of Quantum Mechanics, 1926–1941|journal=[[Physics Today]]|language=en|volume=54|issue=11|pages=56–59|doi=10.1063/1.1428438|bibcode=2001PhT....54k..56M |issn=0031-9228|doi-access=free}}</ref> Rechenberg also co-edited Werner Heisenberg's collected works<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Cassidy|first=David C.|date=June 2003|title=Werner Heisenberg: Gutachten- und Prüfungsprotokolle für Promotionen und Habilitationen (1929–1942)|url=https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/doi/10.1086/379455|journal=Isis|language=en|volume=94|issue=2|pages=390–391|doi=10.1086/379455|issn=0021-1753|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Blum|first1=W.|last2=Dürr|first2=H.-P.|last3=Rechenberg|first3=H.|last4=Telegdi|first4=Valentine L.|last5=Weisskopf|first5=Victor F.|date=July 1991|title=Heisenberg: Gesammelte Werke [Collected Works]|url=http://physicstoday.scitation.org/doi/10.1063/1.2810176|journal=Physics Today|language=en|volume=44|issue=7|pages=55–58|doi=10.1063/1.2810176|bibcode=1991PhT....44g..55B |issn=0031-9228|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and from 1977 headed the MPI's Werner Heisenberg Archive.<ref name=":0" /> After retiring, he wrote a two-volume biography of Heisenberg.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Hentschel|first=Klaus|date=December 2011|title=Die Sprache der Atome. Leben und Wirken – Eine wissenschaftliche Biographie. Die 'Fröhliche Wissenschaft' (Jugend bis Nobelpreis)|url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/product/identifier/S0007087411001166/type/journal_article|journal=The British Journal for the History of Science|language=en|volume=44|issue=4|pages=612–614|doi=10.1017/S0007087411001166|s2cid=147506467 |issn=0007-0874|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

From 1991 to 2006, he was also a board member of the [[Deutsche Physikalische Gesellschaft]]'s Physics History Association.<ref name=":0" />
